title: Wham and giving Glenn Miller half the credit
summary: Wham was written for Moten, reworked for lyricist Taps Miller, and recorded by Glenn Miller in exchange for half the writer credit.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I see that Parnassie -- we mentioned all the ones with Lunceford except Wham. He mentioned Wham was one of the Lunceford's.
Yeah, that was originally made for Benny Moten.

Well, here's the way it was. Taps Miller had the lyrics. He went to Basie, Basie wouldn't do them because they was all out of meter and he didn't have the meters, he couldn't fit the words with the music.

So I listened to it and Tap said, well, I need this band, Basie won't do it. I said, well, I'll fix it so he'll do it. And I made it, and so Glenn Miller was recording, and Glenn gave me two numbers to make up for ____. And I made up -- like, Wham, that went on -- by

me straightening it out for Basie, I said, let me let Glenn play it. And Glenn wouldn't play arrangements with pencil, so I carried in the pencil copy, go over this, let's see. And I say, take it up and I'll have it -- he said, you're not taking this noplace. He say, Glenn took this arrangement, no, you're not getting this. We're going to play this (unintelligible). Say, that's good for ______. I say, yeah, yeah, so that's how they got that.

So and then Taps -- I told Taps, now, anything Glenn does, I gives him 50 percent of the original because his name was big. So it's better to let him have 50 percent of your song, Stanley, than to have it laying up to today and it wouldn't be known.
But he didn't want his name on it. He said, no, no, because he'd been around too long and they'd pick up on the style.
So he said, I'll do the numbers, just give me 50 percent of the writership.
